surfaceForm: The full suite is exercised at minimum once per year.
proposedGenericDecision: A conformance cadence is a governance parameter set by the adopting institution; a hard-coded annual minimum embeds an assumption about the institution's risk appetite, audit calendar, and supervisory regime that does not generalise.
rationale: "At minimum once per year" is a jurisdiction/governance-bound default. It reads reasonably but is a numeric institutional constant rather than an architectural property; safer to expose as a locally-set cadence parameter so a regulated or higher-risk institution can tighten it.

surfaceForm: Participants. One engineer per affected layer, one observability operator (to retrieve replay material), one note-taker, and the operational owner of the scope.
proposedGenericDecision: Describe roles in capability terms (a layer engineer role, an observability/replay role, a recording role, an operational scope owner) so that a small institution where one person fills several roles, or an outsourced-operations institution, can map them; one-FTE-per-layer implies an in-house, sufficiently-staffed organisation.
rationale: The role list presumes enough headcount to dedicate one engineer per layer plus dedicated note-taker/owner. For a down-scaled or managed-service institution this is a staffing assumption. Already role-based, so generalisation (roles may be combined) rather than parameterisation.

surfaceForm: Duration. Indicatively, half a day for a single layer; one day for a full institutional review.
proposedGenericDecision: Keep as an explicitly hedged illustration ("indicatively") tied to institutional scale; optionally note duration scales with the number of instantiated layers and the size of the estate.
rationale: Already softened with "Indicatively" and tied to scope size, so it is close to scale-invariant guidance. Flagged for completeness because the day/half-day figures presume a mid-sized single-campus estate, but the hedge makes it acceptable to keep.

surfaceForm: A smaller or teaching-led institution following the down-scaled profile (\trchap{ch:sizing}{}, \S\ref{sec:sz-downscale}) may legitimately target a steady-state index below 3 on layers it consumes as managed or mutualised services...
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch16-conformance-EN.tex, \section{Reporting template} (\paragraph{The index is a maturity trajectory...})
proposedGenericDecision: This is already a generalisation device (it explicitly accommodates non-research, teaching-led, managed-service institutions). Keep; it is the mechanism that makes the chapter institution-agnostic rather than a leak.
rationale: Positive signal, not specificity. The cross-references to the sizing chapter and down-scale section are the abstraction layer the matrix exercise wants; recorded so reviewers do not mistake it for a UL-bound assumption.

surfaceForm: an artefact that the institution can share with peers in the international network anticipated by this Reference.
proposedGenericDecision: Frame peer-sharing as an optional benefit available to any adopter rather than membership in a specific "international network anticipated by this Reference", which presumes the document's own ecosystem/programme context.
rationale: "the international network anticipated by this Reference" assumes the adopting institution participates in the specific peer network the source suite envisions. For a standalone adopter this is a contextual assumption; soften to "with peer institutions".

surfaceForm: Kubernetes API passes upstream conformance tests on the production cluster. / S3 API operations on the production object store ... / IPFIX flow records ... / HSM key migration ...
proposedGenericDecision: The table presumes the institution self-operates the full nine-layer estate (own cluster, own object store, own HSM, own CA). The reporting section already concedes managed/mutualised layers; ensure the table caption's "illustrative / seed the institution's own" framing covers the case where a layer is consumed as a service and the test becomes a provider exit-term check rather than a self-run test.
rationale: Each row presumes in-house operation of that layer. This is already mitigated twice: the caption marks the suite "illustrative" and the reporting paragraph routes consumed layers to provider exit terms. Logged as an implicit assumption but action is keep given existing hedges.

surfaceForm: Authentication assertion carries the institutional attribute schema, with no captive extensions in the assertion path.
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch16-conformance-EN.tex, \section{Reference test suite per layer} (Identity row, Table~\ref{tab:cf-suite})
proposedGenericDecision: "the institutional attribute schema" is already role-based (whatever schema the adopting institution defines); no UL-specific schema is named. Keep as-is.
rationale: Reviewed for an implied eduGAIN/REFEDS or UL-specific attribute set; the text deliberately stays generic ("institutional attribute schema"). No specificity to remove; recorded as a checked-and-clear item.
